headline: Police used batons and tear gas on garment workers protesting for higher wages in Bangladesh, says HRW
summary: Human Rights Watch urges Bangladeshi authorities to avoid excessive force against garment workers demanding higher wages. The report details police actions, worker demands, and allegations of violence.
details: Human Rights Watch (HRW) has called on Bangladeshi authorities to refrain from using excessive force against garment workers protesting for higher wages. The US-based international human rights organization also urged accountability for those responsible for violence.

In a report released on Thursday, HRW stated that police used batons and tear gas to disperse thousands of garment workers protesting for increased wages. The report also noted incidents of arson, vandalism at factories, and attacks on police during the protests.

Allegations of involvement in the violence have been leveled against individuals associated with factory owners and political parties. HRW emphasized that Bangladeshi authorities must ensure police use force only when necessary and in proportion, in line with international standards.

The protests highlight the workers' demand for a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 Taka, a significant increase from the 12,500 Taka set for 2023. The government has formed a wage board, which is expected to finalize a new wage structure effective from December.

One 31-year-old sewing machine operator shared her struggles, stating, "My house rent is 6,000 Taka. The price of cooking gas is now 2,300 Taka. I get a salary of 13,500 Taka per month. I cannot afford my children's education expenses this year. Tell me, how much money is left for food?"

HRW's report suggests that Bangladeshi authorities are blaming political opponents for inciting protests, rather than addressing the workers' legitimate demands for a living wage. Dhaka Metropolitan Police reported arresting 33 supporters of the ousted Awami League on November 3 for alleged sabotage.

Conversely, members of the ruling party's youth wing have reportedly protested against the demonstrating workers. Three labor leaders were detained in Ashulia on November 3, accused of incitement, and police have filed cases against thousands of unnamed individuals under anti-terrorism laws.

A 28-year-old wife of an arrested individual stated, "They took my husband away. He joined the protest for a short time. He was not involved in any violence." HRW has called for an end to the cycle of violence and impunity surrounding wage negotiations.

International brands also have a role to play. HRW stated that brands must ensure their supply chain contracts do not incentivize worker abuse or make living wages impossible. They must guarantee that contract terms do not encourage worker abuse or make paying a living wage impossible.

headline_marked: Two DGFI members [[dismissed and jailed]] in Mohammadpur extortion case
headline: Two DGFI members dismissed and jailed in Mohammadpur extortion case
summary: Sergeant Al Mamun and Lance Corporal Md Nuruzzaman were sentenced to one year in prison following a court martial.
details: Two members of the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence (DGFI) have been dismissed from service and sentenced to one year in prison each following a court martial.
The convicts, Sergeant Al Mamun and Lance Corporal Md Nuruzzaman, were arrested in October this year after an alleged extortion attempt and assault on a businessman in Dhaka's Mohammadpur.
The victim, motorcycle trader Mohammad Sharif, was allegedly confined in a flat in Chandrima Model Town and demanded to pay Tk 10 lakh.
Sharif had gone to the flat with an Ansar member to purchase a motorcycle, but was instead confined and assaulted.
The businessman had handed over Tk 70,000 before being further threatened. He eventually escaped by spotting a police patrol vehicle at a tea stall in Shyamoli.
Police arrested six people, including the two DGFI personnel, and seized the vehicle used in the crime.
Following their arrest, the two DGFI members were handed over to the army for trial under military law, where the allegations were proved.
caption:
Two DGFI members have been dismissed and sentenced to one year in prison for extorting a businessman.

Two members of the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence (DGFI) have been dismissed from service and sentenced to one year in prison each following a court martial.

The convicts, Sergeant Al Mamun and Lance Corporal Md Nuruzzaman, were arrested in October this year after an alleged extortion attempt and assault on a businessman in Dhaka's Mohammadpur.

The victim, motorcycle trader Mohammad Sharif, was allegedly confined in a flat in Chandrima Model Town and demanded to pay Tk 10 lakh.

Sharif had gone to the flat with an Ansar member to purchase a motorcycle, but was instead confined and assaulted.

The businessman had handed over Tk 70,000 before being further threatened. He eventually escaped by spotting a police patrol vehicle at a tea stall in Shyamoli.

Police arrested six people, including the two DGFI personnel, and seized the vehicle used in the crime.

Following their arrest, the two DGFI members were handed over to the army for trial under military law, where the allegations were proved.
